body:
Working the Bits unit 5 correctly distinguishes decoding fixed-point values from extracting their whole part. The earlier fractions pilot also includes one half-pixel move (learner task 9). It does not provide a repeated-update contrast that shows why a rounded drawing coordinate must not overwrite the stored fractional state.

Prepare one bounded optional paper experiment in the existing unit, using unsigned 16-bit values at scale 256: start position 0, add stored step 128 four times, and draw only the whole part. Compare retaining the stored value with a deliberately labelled variant that writes the extracted whole part back at scale 256 after each draw. Both first draws are 0; the second update distinguishes the policies. Do not describe the correct existing example as broken.

Acceptance:
- Recall scale, state and drawing locally; use existing notation/components and keep system tracks independent.
- Ask for a prediction before the result, with a hint and separate explanation; no scoring gate, new runtime, dependency or new module.
- Show stored state, full decoded position and drawn whole coordinate separately. Preserve the stored fraction between updates.
- Include a quarter-step variation and explicit width/range limits. Do not silently choose wrap, saturation or a signed convention outside the stated domain.
- Retain independent exact-rational/integer model checks, a one-update false positive and nonzero rejection of the wrong retention policy. Reuse accepted target evidence unless a new machine claim needs execution.
- Verify the changed public page's build, keyboard/readability and wide/narrow output. Keep model, target and actual learner results separate.

A prepared paper trial and assessor sheet accompany the evidence-queue docs PR. No learner has tried it; educational effectiveness remains unknown. Continues stevehill1981/198x#114/#115/#124.
title: Trace fractional state across repeated fixed-point updates
